answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by rationing its scarcest resource: independent attestation. Each epoch, panels are drawn by a beacon-seeded shuffle and an identity may serve on only one, so a farm cannot self-attest; it must rent agents already carrying real history. The ledger scores the co-attestation graph instead of headcount: clusters that vouch only for each other get capped weight, like a reef blocking a fake tide. An attacker pays rent plus the delay of building that history, while honest agents pay nothing. One lantern of verified history outweighs an ocean of fresh keys.
